evidence_tree.command: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
evidence_tree.isolation: Only data/** and docs/math-foundations.md were read. src/, tests/, scripts/, docs/plans/, docs/receipts/, the diff and git history were never opened.

semantics_established_from_sources.what_'consume'_is: The rotation receipt's setup/consume edge detection. data/worklists/f2-task.md defines the receipt shape: "The /api/calculate response gains a 'rotation' receipt: {order: [Q,E,E,E,...], rationale: \"Q poisons, E consumes\"}". data/worklists/f3-task.md defines the detector: "DETECT setup/consume edges automatically from the ability rows + module metadata: an ability whose row names indicate application (poison/blemish/stack/mark/amp/slow/root/stun/on-hit) must precede abilities that consume (enhanced/consume/detonate/bonus-vs/X-stack/%missing); read the actual attributes from data/champions.json (e.g. 'Bonus Damage', 'Enhanced', 'Total Enhanced', 'per stack', ...)". So consume[] is the ordered list of Syndra ability slots classified as the CONSUMING side of an edge.
semantics_established_from_sources.what_'derived_order'_is: An engine-derived (non-default) cast order, the same vocabulary used in data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json: "the enemy Ahri's F3-derived order opens with E (charm) instead of Q".
semantics_established_from_sources.what_'60'_is: The pinned Splinters of Wrath stack count for the scenario. Syndra's Transcendent thresholds in the cached wiki text are 40 (Q), 60 (W), 80 (E), 100 (R), 120 (P). 60 is precisely W's threshold, which is what the scenario is built to exercise. The champion-audit cache confirms the option exists: data/champion-audit/batch-e9-1.json, Syndra: "E3 implemented the Transcendent splinter system (splinters option: 120 -> 1.15x AP buff, 40+ Q charges via Q2 slot, 60+ W true damage), R sphere count (r_spheres). All five slots modeled with sourced numbers."

step_1_thresholds_live_at_60_splinters.Q_40: MET  - 'Transcendent Bonus: Collecting 40 Splinters of Wrath causes Syndra to periodically stock a Dark Sphere charge, up to a maximum of 2.' (60 >= 40)
step_1_thresholds_live_at_60_splinters.W_60: MET  - 'Transcendent Bonus: Collecting 60 Splinters of Wrath enhances Force of Will to deal 12% (+ 2% per 100 AP) bonus true damage.' The wording is 'Collecting 60', i.e. the threshold is inclusive at exactly 60.

step_2_W_carries_an_'enhanced'_consume_r.text_signal: The W Transcendent Bonus effect literally uses the detector's keyword: 'enhances Force of Will'.
step_2_W_carries_an_'enhanced'_consume_r.attribute_row_signal: The cached W leveling rows carry the attribute names 'Bonus True Damage' and 'Total Mixed Damage' - i.e. exactly the 'Bonus Damage' / 'Total ...' attribute family f3-task.md names as consume-side markers. No other Syndra slot has a bonus/total-enhanced row.
step_2_W_carries_an_'enhanced'_consume_r.arithmetic_cross_check: Cached 'Bonus True Damage' values = [8.4, 12, 15.6, 19.2, 22.8]; cached W base 'Magic Damage' values = [70, 100, 130, 160, 190]. 0.12 x [70,100,130,160,190] = [8.4, 12, 15.6, 19.2, 22.8] - exact match, confirming these rows are the 12% enhancement, not an unrelated row. Cached 'Total Mixed Damage' = [78.4, 112, 145.6, 179.2, 212.8] = base x 1.12, exact match again. The enhancement is therefore real, quantified, and gated at 60 splinters.

step_3_W_also_carries_a_threshold_indepe.setup_side_Q: 'Active: Syndra conjures a Dark Sphere at the target location ... The Dark Sphere then remains on the ground for 6 seconds.' (Q is the sphere producer.)
step_3_W_also_carries_a_threshold_indepe.consume_side_W: 'Active: Syndra telekinetically grabs the nearest Dark Sphere, enemy minion or non-epic monster within 500 units from the target location, and holds the target near her for 5 seconds. If a Dark Sphere is grabbed, its duration is refreshed ... She prioritizes grabbing the nearest unit, then Dark Spheres.' W cannot deal its damage without an object to grab; the in-kit source of that object is Q's Dark Sphere. That is a textbook setup(Q) -> consume(W) edge, independent of any splinter count.
step_3_W_also_carries_a_threshold_indepe.peer_consistency: The two slots that are in the old 3-entry list on the same grounds consume spheres no more strongly than W does: E - 'Dark Spheres can be knocked back for 950 units ...' (uses a Q sphere), R - 'Syndra conjures 3 Dark Spheres and additionally grabs up to 4 nearby live ones' (uses live Q spheres). A consume set that contains E and R but omits W is internally inconsistent: W is the single most sphere-dependent ability in the kit.

expected_consume_slots: R (grabs up to 4 live Q Dark Spheres)
W (60-splinter enhancement MET + grabs a Q Dark Sphere)
step_4_expected_set_and_cardinality_at_6.cardinality: 4 entries -> valid indices 0..3. The old baseline had exactly 3 entries (index 3 absent) and the new baseline has 4 with 'W' appended at index 3; indices 0-2 are unchanged, consistent with W being the only slot added.
step_4_expected_set_and_cardinality_at_6.conclusion: W must be present. The old baseline's omission is only defensible if the 60-splinter gate were evaluated strictly (> 60) or if W's grab-a-sphere dependency were ignored; the cached wiki text supports neither - it says 'Collecting 60 Splinters of Wrath enhances Force of Will', and it says W 'grabs the nearest Dark Sphere'.

sources_quoted.relevance: Confirms the rotation family is a scheduled cast-order construct; math-foundations contains no Syndra-specific or splinter-threshold statement, so the threshold arithmetic rests entirely on the cached wiki text above.

caveats: The golden baseline file itself and the resolver source were not read (runbook isolation), so the exact contents of consume[0..2] are inferred from the leaf diff (only index 3 changed) rather than observed. This does not affect the verdict, which is about whether 'W' belongs in the consume set at 60 splinters.

If the engine's consume list were instead intended to hold only threshold-gated slots, W is still required at 60 (its gate is exactly 60 and is inclusive). If it holds sphere-consumption edges, W is still required (it grabs a Dark Sphere). Both readings agree, which is why the verdict is unambiguous.
